cards.headline: Former gang leader convicted of murdering Tupac Shakur in 1996
cards.teaser: A Las Vegas jury found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of first-degree murder for orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur. The jury reached its verdict in approximatel
cards.body:
A Las Vegas jury found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of first-degree murder for orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur. The jury reached its verdict in approximately three hours, bringing closure to a case that remained unsolved for nearly 30 years.

Davis, a 63-year-old former South Side Compton Crips gang leader, did not pull the trigger himself but was accused of planning and commanding the drive-by shooting. Prosecutors argued he orchestrated the attack in retaliation after Shakur's entourage attacked Davis's nephew, Orlando "Baby Lane" Anderson, earlier that evening at the Mike Tyson-Bruce Seldon fight.

The shooting occurred on September 7, 1996, when a Cadillac pulled up next to Shakur's vehicle near the Las Vegas strip and fired eight shots. Shakur was hospitalized but died days later from his injuries. The case had frustrated law enforcement and captivated hip-hop fans for three decades, spawning countless theories and investigations.

During the two-week trial, prosecutors presented evidence including video footage and audio recordings of Davis describing his alleged role in the incident. Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal told jurors: "Let's be clear, Duane Davis did not pull the trigger. But he did plan the shooting in retaliation of the beating of his nephew." The prosecution's case relied heavily on Davis's own admissions, made through years of statements to investigators and interviews.

Davis's defense attorney Michael Sanft argued that after 30 years, authorities possessed very little credible evidence. Sanft suggested that when Davis previously spoke with law enforcement agencies including the FBI, investigators did not pursue his claims because they questioned their credibility.

A major factor in the case was Davis's 2019 memoir, in which he detailed his involvement in the shooting. Prosecutors said the book ultimately revived the Las Vegas investigation. Defense attorneys attempted to exclude the memoir from trial, arguing Davis and his co-author had exaggerated details to place himself at the center of events for personal gain. A judge denied this request.

The jury comprised six men and ten women selected the previous week. During opening arguments, witness testimony came from Garry Dale, a former Las Vegas officer who had stopped Shakur's vehicle before the shooting, and Ingrid Stokes, a woman in a nearby car who heard the gunshots.

Shakur, killed at age 25, was one of rap's most influential artists and a cultural icon. His death, alongside the subsequent killing of rival rapper Notorious B.I.G., became emblematic of the East Coast-West Coast hip-hop rivalry of the 1990s.

Davis faces sentencing following his conviction. The guilty verdict represents the first successful prosecution in a case that had remained open throughout the lives of an entire generation of hip-hop fans.

cards.headline: Dolly Parton buried in Nashville following private family funeral
cards.teaser: Country music legend Dolly Parton was laid to rest in Nashville alongside her husband following a private family funeral. The singer died on Tuesday at the age of 80 after sufferin
cards.body:
Country music legend Dolly Parton was laid to rest in Nashville alongside her husband following a private family funeral. The singer died on Tuesday at the age of 80 after suffering from cancer.

Parton's death marks the loss of one of the most celebrated and influential figures in American music history. Over a career spanning more than six decades, she became known for her distinctive voice and songwriting, but also for her humanitarian work and business ventures.

The private ceremony reflects the family's desire for an intimate farewell to the entertainer who had touched millions of lives. Parton had been married to Carl Dean, who remained largely out of the public eye throughout their decades-long marriage.

Parton possessed a distinctive soprano with a remarkable vibrato and east Tennessee twang that made her voice among the most recognizable in music. Her wit was equally famous, with self-deprecating humor that endeared her to audiences worldwide. Her maxim "It takes a lot of money to look this cheap" captured her appetite for glitz and mischief that defined her public persona.

She was a pioneering figure in taking country music into the mainstream, becoming one of the first country stars to achieve significant crossover success. At the 2014 Glastonbury festival, she attracted what was reportedly the largest crowd in the event's history, performing while wearing a crystal-studded white suit and tooting a rhinestone saxophone.

Her songwriting prowess earned her recognition across the industry, with 10 Grammy awards, 11 from the Academy of Country Music, and numerous other honors. Her composition "I Will Always Love You" became one of the best-selling singles of all time after Whitney Houston recorded it for "The Bodyguard" soundtrack in 1992. The song earned Parton enough money, she said, "to buy Graceland" and proved that her refusal to share publishing rights with Elvis Presley when he wanted to record it had been the right decision.

Beyond music, Parton's charitable work reflected her commitment to helping others. From 1988, she provided support to local schoolchildren, and from 1995, she ran an international book reading programme. She also provided aid for people affected by wildfires and hurricanes and supported medical research. Her Imagination Library became known worldwide for distributing free books to millions of children, inspired in part by her father's inability to read.

Though known for her glamorous exterior and larger-than-life persona, Parton grounded her public image with deep intelligence and honesty. She remained active in her career and charitable work until recent years, leaving behind a lasting impact on generations of musicians who followed in her footsteps and a legacy that extended far beyond music into film, television, and popular culture.

cards.headline: Dolly Parton Dies
cards.teaser: Country music legend Dolly Parton has died at age 80 following a battle with cancer, according to reports released this week. The singer, songwriter, actress, and philanthropist wa
cards.body:
Country music legend Dolly Parton has died at age 80 following a battle with cancer, according to reports released this week. The singer, songwriter, actress, and philanthropist was one of the most influential figures in American entertainment, with a career that transformed country music and extended far beyond the genre.

Parton rose to prominence in the 1960s after moving to Nashville at 18 to pursue a recording career. She quickly became a songwriter for Combine Publishing before signing with Monument Records as an artist. Her early career included eight years as a television personality on Porter Wagoner's popular variety show starting in 1967, though her solo recordings initially outsold her duets with Wagoner.

Her breakthrough came after leaving Wagoner in 1974. She wrote "I Will Always Love You" as a farewell to him, and the song became a signature hit. The track gained international recognition when Whitney Houston recorded it for the 1992 film "The Bodyguard," becoming one of the best-selling singles ever made. Parton's refusal to cede publishing rights to the song, even when Elvis Presley requested them, proved to be a pivotal decision.

With a distinctive soprano voice featuring a remarkable vibrato and east Tennessee twang, Parton became Nashville's most recognized female export. Her catalog of hits included "Jolene" and numerous other songs that explored themes of love, loss, and female empowerment. Over her lifetime, she earned 10 Grammy Awards, 11 Academy of Country Music Awards, and many other accolades.

Beyond music, Parton built a substantial business empire. She starred in films including "9 to 5" and "Steel Magnolias," and established Dollywood, the theme park in Tennessee that became a major attraction.

Parton's charitable contributions defined much of her later life. She founded the Imagination Library in 1995, a program that has distributed free books to millions of children worldwide, inspired by her father's inability to read. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she donated one million dollars to vaccine research at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. She also provided aid to people affected by wildfires and hurricanes.

Known for her wit and maximalist approach to life, Parton became a cultural icon whose appeal transcended generational and genre boundaries. Her distinctive style, featuring her signature platinum hair and elaborate fashion choices, made her a fashion icon in her own right. She was one of the first country stars to achieve mainstream crossover success, playing a major role in bringing country music to wider audiences.

Tributes have poured in from across the entertainment, music, and political worlds, celebrating her lasting impact on culture and her generous spirit.

cards.headline: Country Music Icon Dolly Parton Dies
cards.teaser: Dolly Parton, the legendary country music singer, songwriter, and actress, has died at age 80. Her family announced that she passed away in Nashville after bravely facing a brief b
cards.body:
Dolly Parton, the legendary country music singer, songwriter, and actress, has died at age 80. Her family announced that she passed away in Nashville after bravely facing a brief battle with cancer at Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center, surrounded by loved ones. Her nephew Bryan Seaver shared a statement saying, "She never saw a door she couldn't open, and the doors she opened made and changed history." Per her wishes, her funeral will be small and private.

In a recent interview, Parton had mentioned dealing with health issues while caring for her husband Carl Dean, who died in March last year. She expressed her determination to continue working, saying, "I still have so many things I want to achieve, so I'm gonna keep on working as long as I can to see everything come to life."

Parton rose from poverty in Tennessee to become a cultural icon and prolific songwriter, writing 3,000 songs including hits like "Jolene" and "9 to 5." She built a career spanning more than six decades and achieved success as an actress, appearing in major Hollywood films. Beyond entertainment, she became an accomplished businesswoman with ventures ranging from the Dollywood theme park to cosmetics and baking mixes.

Her philanthropic work was equally impressive. The Dollywood Foundation distributes approximately 25 million books annually through her Imagination Library across the US, Canada, Australia, the UK and Ireland. She also donated one million dollars for COVID-19 vaccine research, which formed the basis for the Moderna vaccine.

Following news of her death, tributes poured in from across music, film, and politics. Jane Fonda, her co-star in "9 to 5," wrote an emotional Instagram post, describing Parton as "the voluptuous embodiment of empathy" and noting that "more than anyone I have ever known, Dolly will always be with us because she was so present, so powerful, so generous and playful."

Billy Ray Cyrus, whose daughter Miley is Parton's goddaughter, shared memories of meeting her in 1992 and recalled her recent message telling him she loved him with her whole heart. Pitbull performed at a concert in New York, calling Parton "a good human being with a good heart" who believed in him when others didn't.

Other celebrities paying tribute included Beyonce, Paul McCartney, Elton John, and Christina Aguilera. The White House lowered its flag to half-mast in her honor.

In Tennessee, Governor Bill Lee announced plans to rename Nashville International Airport after Parton as a lasting tribute to the entertainer who maintained deep ties to her home state throughout her life. Searches for Dolly Parton merchandise surged dramatically following her death, with online searches for T-shirts increasing by 10,000 percent as fans sought ways to commemorate her legacy.

President Donald Trump will fly to Ireland next week aboard a Boeing 747 gifted by Qatar, despite ongoing security concerns about the aircraft. Plans to take the plane out of service for security upgrades have been pushed back to later this fall.

The decision to use the Qatari-gifted aircraft for international travel raises questions about the readiness of the plane for presidential use. Security upgrades that officials had planned to implement before the aircraft entered regular service will now be delayed until after the Ireland visit.

The Boeing 747 was a gift from Qatar to the United States. Presidential aircraft typically undergo extensive modifications and security enhancements before being cleared for use in transporting the president on foreign trips. The standard security protocols for presidential travel include advanced communications systems, defensive countermeasures, and other classified protections.

The Ireland trip marks one of Trump's first major international visits since the escalation of tensions in the Middle East, including the ongoing conflict with Iran that has affected oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz. The decision to proceed with the trip using the unupgraded aircraft suggests the White House views the security measures currently in place as sufficient for the journey.

The postponement of security upgrades until later this fall means the aircraft will continue flying in its current configuration for at least several more weeks. cards.headline: Supreme Court rules political parties entitled to lower TV ad rates
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court delivered a significant victory to Republican and Democratic party organizations Friday, ruling that political parties are entitled to discounted television adver
cards.body:
The Supreme Court delivered a significant victory to Republican and Democratic party organizations Friday, ruling that political parties are entitled to discounted television advertising rates when they coordinate spending with candidates.

The decision addresses a long-standing dispute over how broadcast stations must price political advertising under federal communications law. Broadcasters are required to offer candidates the lowest unit rate for ad time during the weeks before an election, but questions have persisted about whether this rule applies to party committees that coordinate with campaigns. The court's ruling extends these discounted rates to party organizations, potentially saving national and state party committees millions of dollars in advertising costs.

The timing of the decision comes as both major parties prepare for the 2026 midterm elections in November, when control of Congress and numerous state offices will be decided. Political advertising spending for the 2026 cycle is expected to reach record levels, with television continuing to serve as a dominant medium even as digital platforms grow in importance. Party committees, which are permitted to raise larger contributions than individual candidates under federal law, play a crucial role in funding competitive races across the country.

The ruling could substantially reshape the financial landscape of campaign advertising by making party-funded television spots significantly less expensive during the critical final weeks leading up to elections. Television stations had opposed the extension, arguing that providing lowest unit rates to coordinated party spending would reduce their advertising revenue and create administrative difficulties. Campaign finance reform advocates have raised concerns that the decision could strengthen the influence of party organizations over individual candidates.

The Supreme Court has not yet released the complete opinion or provided details about the vote breakdown. Legal experts anticipate that the ruling will encourage parties to shift more resources toward traditional broadcast advertising in competitive markets, particularly in swing states and districts where television can reach large numbers of voters who might be persuadable.

The decision addresses a fundamental question about how federal communications law applies to party spending when it is coordinated with candidates. Broadcasters maintain strict pricing rules designed to ensure that candidates have access to affordable advertising, but the precise scope of these requirements has been contested when party organizations make related purchases.

Political parties have long sought equal treatment with candidates under advertising rate regulations. The court's decision validates their argument that coordinated party spending should qualify for the same favorable pricing that candidates receive. This ruling could accelerate a significant shift in how campaign funds are allocated and spent, with parties potentially redirecting resources from other activities to maximize their television advertising capacity during crucial election periods.

cards.headline: Congress delays government funding and Iran war money until after midterms
cards.teaser: Republican lawmakers have voted to postpone major legislative decisions until after the November midterm elections, setting up a crowded agenda for the final weeks of the year. The
cards.body:
Republican lawmakers have voted to postpone major legislative decisions until after the November midterm elections, setting up a crowded agenda for the final weeks of the year. The House overwhelmingly passed a bill to temporarily fund the government, pushing the deadline past Election Day and into the lame-duck session.

The postponed items include government funding, additional money for the ongoing conflict with Iran, and the extension of expanded surveillance authorities. GOP leaders chose to avoid these potentially divisive votes in the weeks leading up to the election, when control of the House hangs in the balance.

The decision creates a compressed timeline between the election and the Christmas recess, when lawmakers will need to address multiple high-stakes issues simultaneously. The lame-duck period, when some members will have already lost their seats or be preparing to leave office, typically makes legislative negotiations more challenging.

The strategy reflects the political sensitivity of these issues in an election year. Government funding debates often lead to shutdown threats, while votes on war spending and surveillance powers can divide both parties. By postponing these votes, Republican leadership aims to avoid giving Democratic challengers ammunition in competitive races.

The Iran war funding has become increasingly urgent as the conflict escalates. The U.S. has launched new airstrikes on Iranian targets, prompting counter strikes by Tehran targeting American interests in multiple locations in the Middle East, including intense ballistic missile attacks on U.S. bases. President Trump warned after Tuesday's U.S. strikes that any Iranian retaliation would be met with responses at "a much harder and higher level."

The escalating exchange of attacks has intensified concerns about a wider renewal of hostilities in the region. Russia's Vladimir Putin has signaled unwavering support for Iran, with Tehran thanking Moscow for backing amid the escalating Middle East war.

The surveillance authorities in question are set to expire, and their extension has drawn opposition from privacy advocates within both parties. Congressional leaders will need to navigate these competing pressures in a shortened timeframe after voters have already rendered their verdict on the current Congress.

The bloated lame-duck agenda will be difficult to complete by Christmas, according to congressional observers. The decision to delay these major decisions reflects the political calculations of Republican leadership heading into the midterm elections, but creates significant challenges for legislative action once the election results are determined.

cards.body:
A federal official has warned that a hastily implemented U.S. Postal Service online system connected to President Trump's mail voting order could reject large batches of ballots ahead of the midterm elections. The whistleblower claims the USPS is rolling out the portal without sufficient testing or safeguards, creating concerns about potential disruptions to voting access.

The online system is being developed in response to Trump's efforts to restrict mail voting. According to the whistleblower, the accelerated timeline could result in technical failures that prevent eligible voters from receiving or submitting their ballots. The official stated that the implementation could potentially "derail" the midterm election if courts allow the plan to move forward.

The USPS portal would represent a significant change to how mail-in voting is processed. The system's design and operational readiness have become central concerns as the midterm elections approach. The whistleblower's allegations indicate that the agency is prioritizing speed over reliability in launching the new technology.

The warning emerges as courts consider challenges to Trump's mail voting restrictions. If legal challenges are unsuccessful and the portal proceeds as planned, election administrators could encounter unprecedented complications when processing absentee ballots. The potential for widespread ballot rejections raises important questions about voter access and election integrity.

Election officials, voting rights advocates, and lawmakers will likely examine the USPS implementation plans closely in the coming weeks. The outcome could affect millions of voters who depend on mail-in ballots, particularly in states with substantial absentee voting populations.

The situation highlights broader concerns about the implementation of voting systems and the importance of adequate testing before launch. Election experts generally emphasize that new voting infrastructure requires extensive preparation and validation to ensure it functions reliably when it matters most.

The USPS has not publicly responded to the whistleblower's claims. The agency typically coordinates with state election officials on mail delivery matters, and any changes to voting procedures would likely require coordination across multiple jurisdictions.

Election administrators in various states have expressed interest in understanding the details of any new USPS procedures. States manage their own voting systems, and changes at the federal level could create complications if they are not clearly communicated and tested beforehand.

The controversy adds uncertainty to the upcoming midterms at a time when election officials are already managing complex logistics. The potential technical issues identified by the whistleblower underscore the need for thorough testing and clear communication between federal agencies and state election officials before new systems go live.

cards.headline: Carlson calls for Trump removal over nuclear weapons consideration
cards.teaser: Tucker Carlson, a prominent conservative podcaster, stated on Friday that President Trump should be removed from office immediately if he is actively considering the first use of n
cards.body:
Tucker Carlson, a prominent conservative podcaster, stated on Friday that President Trump should be removed from office immediately if he is actively considering the first use of nuclear weapons. Carlson said that even contemplating such action should disqualify any president from serving.

"The second any president actively considers the first use of nuclear weapons, that person should be removed from office immediately," Carlson said during his podcast.

The comments represent a notable departure from typical conservative media support for Trump. Carlson framed the issue as a fundamental question of presidential fitness rather than as a partisan political attack. His remarks come amid ongoing discussions about the scope of presidential war powers and military operations in the Middle East.

The source material provided does not specify what prompted Carlson's statement or whether he possesses direct knowledge of Trump considering nuclear options. The White House has not commented on the remarks.

Recent developments in the Trump administration's foreign policy include a nuclear cooperation agreement signed with Saudi Arabia. Under the deal, the kingdom would be enabled to enrich its own uranium for nuclear reactors. At a House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing, Democratic Congressman Brad Sherman called for an oversight hearing of the agreement, suggesting the technology transfer could be as significant a mistake as arming the Shah of Iran during the 1970s.

The specifics of the Saudi Arabia agreement remain unclear until the full text is released. Initial reports suggest it could allow uranium enrichment in Saudi Arabia, potentially opening a pathway to nuclear weapons development in the kingdom. This contrasts with a similar 2009 agreement between the Obama administration and the United Arab Emirates, which included safeguards preventing the Emirates from developing nuclear weapons and committed the country to accepting International Atomic Energy Agency inspections.

Presidential authority over nuclear weapons has been an ongoing subject of legal and policy debate. Some lawmakers have proposed legislation requiring congressional approval before any first use of nuclear weapons. Currently, no such restrictions exist, leaving the decision solely with the president.

Carlson's statement adds a new dimension to political discussions as attention focuses on Trump's second term. Republican figures have largely avoided criticizing Trump on national security matters, making Carlson's position particularly notable within conservative circles. Whether his comments reflect broader concerns among conservatives or represent an isolated view remains unclear.

The Trump administration has been active on multiple fronts, including signing the defense policy bill and conducting military operations in the Middle East. The administration has also reportedly been pushing various policy initiatives affecting voting restrictions and other domestic matters.

cards.headline: Iran war reaches six-month mark with no clear exit strategy
cards.teaser: The war with Iran entered its seventh month with President Trump's path to ending the conflict remaining uncertain. Trump had originally projected a four to five week military camp
cards.body:
The war with Iran entered its seventh month with President Trump's path to ending the conflict remaining uncertain. Trump had originally projected a four to five week military campaign when the war began in late February, but the operation has evolved into an extended engagement centered on economic pressure and control of the Strait of Hormuz.

The war began with goals of degrading Iran's missile capabilities and destroying what remained of its nuclear program. Over six months, the focus has shifted to an open-ended fight over the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for global energy transport. U.S. officials say they have steadily eroded Iran's leverage over the strait in recent months, with the American military gaining what officials describe as the upper hand in the battle for control.

Trump's proposed exits from the conflict have ranged from military victory to a negotiated peace deal tied to reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The war now centers on an economic squeeze of Iran, while the U.S. moves increasing amounts of oil out of the strait to reduce Iranian leverage. Iran and Oman are engaged in some form of negotiations, though the status and prospects of those talks remain in flux.

The extended conflict has become a major feature of Trump's second term, affecting his standing with voters domestically and the U.S. position in the Middle East. Trump is scheduled to visit NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, where his ambitious space priorities are also facing challenges from a divided Republican Congress.

What began as a targeted campaign to address Iran's nuclear and missile programs has transformed into a protracted struggle over regional control and energy security, with no clear timeline for resolution. The war has now lasted more than twelve times longer than the president's initial estimate.

cards.headline: Republicans split over pre-election economic stimulus as growth slows
cards.teaser: House Republicans are divided over whether to pursue economic stimulus legislation before the November midterm elections as new federal data shows slowing economic growth and persi
cards.body:
House Republicans are divided over whether to pursue economic stimulus legislation before the November midterm elections as new federal data shows slowing economic growth and persistent inflation. House Majority Leader Steve Scalise of Louisiana floated the possibility of a fourth budget reconciliation bill last month, but the proposal has exposed disagreements within the party about the best path forward.

The debate comes as Republicans face pressure to show voters they are addressing economic concerns ahead of Election Day. Federal economic indicators have shown the economy is losing momentum while inflation remains elevated, creating political challenges for candidates seeking to defend their economic record or criticize the current administration.

The internal Republican divide reflects broader tensions over fiscal policy and campaign strategy. Some members favor aggressive action to demonstrate responsiveness to economic conditions, while others worry about the political and policy implications of rushing major legislation through Congress in the final weeks before voters head to the polls.

Scalise's trial balloon represents an attempt to find common ground within the Republican caucus on economic messaging. Budget reconciliation, which allows legislation to pass the Senate with a simple majority rather than the usual 60-vote threshold, has been used three times already. A fourth round would require coordination between House and Senate leadership and agreement on policy priorities.

The outcome of these internal discussions could shape both the legislative agenda for the remainder of the congressional session and the economic messages Republicans carry into the midterm elections. With the economy showing signs of weakness, the decision whether to pursue new stimulus measures represents a significant strategic choice for the party as it seeks to maintain or expand its position in Congress.
